description: Crop an image before it's sent: drag, pinch or use the keyboard to move and zoom it under a square, round or 16:9 frame, and turn it a quarter at a time. Linked to a file input or file upload, it hands over the cropped file in place of the picked one, upright whatever the photo's EXIF orientation, scaled to a maximum size and without its EXIF data, so upload-url and Livewire only ever send the crop. Or, given a stored image, it sends the crop's coordinates for the server to cut.

consider.note: The cropped file is made in the browser, so a request can send any file instead. Validate it as an image on the server (`image`, `mimes:`, `dimensions:`) and re-encode it before storing, which also drops anything hidden in it.

Cropping on the server opens the whole image in memory: about 4 bytes a pixel, so 190 MB for a 48-megapixel photo. Check its size with `getimagesize()` before decoding and refuse what's too large, and crop in a queued job if it's slow.
